subject: africanElephant
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: adult African bush elephant.
Style: low-poly.
reasoning:
Adult elephant size needs consideration; a shoulder height of approximately 3.2 meters seems appropriate for this stylized representation. The elephant's base should align with y=0 to establish a grounded visual presence.


The model will be oriented with +Z forward, +Y up, and centered at the origin, defining the base rest pose including the skeleton and rigging elements like limbs, trunk, ears, tail, and jaw. A low-poly style with a faceted appearance and a focus on silhouette will be used, employing the available tools to achieve a stylized, detailed, and expressive representation, incorporating elements such as wrinkles, mud, and a savanna-themed base. The model will adhere to specified part, triangle, joint, and color limits.


A detailed anatomical reference for the African Bush Elephant is being created, focusing on key visual traits such as the saddle back, ear shape, tusks, trunk with two "fingers," domed forehead, leg structure, wrinkled hide, and tail. Skeleton planning begins by establishing root positions (hips or core) and defining a spine chain with key points for pelvis, saddle dip, high shoulder, neck base, head/skull, and jaw joint. The trunk will be modeled as a chain stemming from the nose/upper lip.


Tusks and ears will be articulated via joints for movement. Leg joint positions are defined, with the right side mirrored from the left.  Tail length and joint count established.

Scale is calibrated based on a real-world elephant of roughly 2.65m shoulder height, with the overall dimensions derived from that, including tusk and ear dimensions, and total length. Low-poly art direction emphasizes blocky primitives with stylized details, color, and composition.


Faceted sweeps and extrusions are essential for the low-poly aesthetic, focusing on capturing the silhouette with angular sections and crisp bevels. The trunk and tusks will utilize faceted forms to enhance the origami/chiseled effect, with the torso sculpted using a combination of lofts and layered volumes for the heavy build. Procedural paints will be crafted to simulate dried mud and cracked elephant hide, incorporating Worley noise for wrinkles and reddish-orange laterite dust.


A base color and highlights are chosen for the hide, with mud splatters added at the feet for realism. Tusk texture will be based on polished ivory with a darker, stained base near the gums.

The ears will be shaped like Africa, with internal details like blood vessels. Head features include forehead lobes, temporal hollows, and a detailed eye with wrinkles, using an anime/stylized eye decal or custom texture. The trunk's rings and two finger projections will be included, with a triangular lower jaw.


Details for knee and wrist knuckles are being incorporated, alongside massive, flat-bottomed foot pads with rounded toenails. The tail's tapered shape and coarse end brush are being defined.

A stylized savanna diorama base is planned, featuring a rocky pedestal, scattered rocks, golden grass, and either a fallen log or termite mound. The base aims to frame the model.

Confirmation of import, export, random number generator, and part/triangle/joint/color limits have been reviewed. Ensuring the lowest point of the model touches the ground is also confirmed.


Base coordinates and anatomical landmarks are established for the elephant model, including foot positions, withers, hip height, and spine curvature, ensuring the model's bottom rests at ground level. Detailed trunk and tusk coordinates are defined with sweeping curves, and the jaw joint is positioned to provide realistic proportions. The trunk's length and tusk placements are checked for a dynamic and imposing presence.


A low-poly torso can be constructed using a series of stations along the spine, employing a lofting tool. Station dimensions and positions are being defined to capture the elephant's barrel-like ribcage, drooping belly, saddle back, and prominent withers. Faceted sections with specified sides create the desired chiseled, low-poly appearance.


Adding faceted shoulder and hip plates to accentuate muscular planes is being considered. Using slabs or frustum boxes, placed at specific coordinates relative to the withers and pelvis, will define these forms.  Leg design is being planned with vertical columns reflecting the elephant's graviportal limbs. Coordinates for front and hind leg joints are established, with geometry defined as tapered columns for the upper legs and cylindrical pads for the feet.


Joint positions for the leg, ankle, and foot pad are being established. Leg geometry will be defined using tapered and cylindrical primitives; the upper leg radius is specified as a variable to control proportions. The number of toenails and their angular placement on the foot rims are being determined to enhance realism.

Head construction is starting by analyzing skull geometry; temporal ridges, forehead slope, temporal fossa, cheekbones, eye sockets, and premaxillary bones are being assessed as key anatomical features. Now contemplating use of a region tool for head construction.


Defined head joint and cranial features, including mirrored domes, a main skull block, forehead plane, cheek wedges, and tusk root sheaths. Established lower jaw joint parameters, shape as a tapered wedge, and included internal mouth details. Planned trunk geometry as a faceted low-poly sweep with a tapering radius and lifelike curve.


Considering adding low-poly ring ridges to the trunk, along with procedural wrinkles. Identified distinct dorsal and ventral "fingers" at the trunk tip, each as small wedges. Two nostril recesses are also included.

Tusks will be modeled with a tapered sweep, defined by a series of coordinates. The tusk's radius will taper significantly from base to tip.  Planned for ivory-colored paint with a darker base and a polished tip.


Ears will be shaped with a custom extrusion following the outline of the African continent, incorporating natural edge details and a tapered thickness. Ear joints will be established with specified coordinates and angled outward. Veins will be simulated using branching sweeps or low-poly tubes, with a low-poly ear canal entrance.

Eyes are planned to be set into the skull at defined coordinates and angles. The eye will be a dark sphere with an amber iris, horizontal pupil, and a warm highlight. Heavy upper eyelids and concentric wrinkle arches will be included to convey a wise expression. The tail will be long and slender.


Tail joint positions and shape are being defined, including a faceted tapered sweep for the shaft and layered blades for the hair brush at the tip. A low-poly, irregular terrain base for the savanna is planned, with faceted shapes and sunbaked soil colors. Footprints will be added along with scattered rocks, a fallen branch, grass tufts, and a termite mound. The elephant skin material will use a slate grey base color.


Wrinkled hide will be simulated using a cellular pattern with darkened creases and dusty centers, and blended with dust and mud based on height and normals. Ear coloration will differentiate back and front, with pinkish-buff inner areas fading to grey. Tusks will be rendered with a gradient from weathered brown base to polished ivory tip.

Part and triangle counts were estimated for each component, including the body, legs, trunk, tusks, head, ears, tail, and base, to ensure the model adheres to constraints.


Component part counts are estimated; the elephant model should stay within the 1000 part constraint, with the base props adding approximately 30 parts. Triangle counts for the model parts are expected to be well within the 60,000 triangle limit.

A bone hierarchy and rig key is verified, defining the parent-child relationships for all skeletal elements, including spine, head, tail, and legs, and their respective roles, such as spine, leg, and tentacle. Ground contact calculations confirmed the model's lowest point is aligned with y = 0.00, ensuring a grounded presence.


A ground-framing base will be added with a slightly recessed footprint at a negative Y offset, ensuring the elephant model sits atop the terrain. Helper functions are planned for low-poly primitives such as toenails, trunk rings, ear veins, rocks, termite mounds, acacia branches, and savanna grass. Verification of all import functions from the available toolkit is underway.


Eye decal placement determined based on skull flank coordinates. Ear outline established using a series of 2D points, capturing African elephant silhouette, thickness, bevel, and extrusion parameters. Tusk modeling commenced with coordinates for base and path points defining its curved shape.


Analyzing coordinates and curve data to construct the tusk's faceted form, aiming for a low-poly aesthetic resembling carved ivory. Observed a downward then upward sweep in tusk geometry; these findings will be used to generate the correct curve with specified radius and facet count.

Proceeded to model cranial lobes using dodecahedrons; additional features include a forehead plate, temporal hollows, and brow ridges. These features will define the head's profile.

Lower jaw geometry defined as a faceted frustum box, connected at a specific joint; a triangular under-lip pad was included. Trunk is defined using a seven-joint chain, establishing a base path for its construction.


Defined trunk geometry using a sweep with a dynamic radius based on progression, incorporating seven-sided facets for a low-poly style. Added 12-14 faceted ring details to the trunk, along with two finger projections and nostril recesses.

Established the tail as a four-joint chain, utilizing a defined curve and tapering radius for its construction.  Planned a faceted brush at the tail tip, with radiating dark bristles.

Defined front leg components: a shoulder socket, faceted upper and lower leg columns, ankle column, and a cylindrical foot pad precisely positioned at ground level.  The front foot pad is perfectly touching the floor.


Defined hind leg geometry using coordinate-based column primitives, including thigh, lower leg, and hock. Foot pad constructed using a cylinder, positioned to meet the ground plane with defined toenail angles.

Established the footprint parameters on the base, encompassing leg coordinates, width, and overall base dimensions, along with the ground slab's height and polygonal properties. The termite mound, acacia log, and savanna rocks are now considered for the scene.


The savanna base elements are being planned, including placement of rocks, a log, grass clusters, and a termite mound to frame the elephant model.  A procedural skin material, `ELEPHANT_SKIN`, is being developed, utilizing a base gray color, cell-based wrinkles, savanna dust application, mud for the lower legs, and a lighter belly.  Color palettes are chosen for the elephant's inner ear, ivory tusks, savanna base, termite mound, acacia wood, and savanna grass, each aiming for a realistic yet stylized aesthetic. Further verification of the modeling approach is completed.
